name: phantom-write-claim-repeated
doc: FANG-9, the branch where the guard has to speak for itself. Step 0 is the same unbacked write claim as phantom-write-claim; step 1 is the model REPEATING it after the runtime's challenge instead of calling file_write or admitting anything. That is the only path that produces the [Unverified] note, and on the streaming route it is the path that exposed the ordering defect: the driver emits ContentComplete — which /api/agents/{id}/message/stream publishes as `event: done` — the instant the model stops talking, so the first version of this patch pushed its retraction out AFTER the client had been told the turn was over. A consumer that treats `done` as the end of the turn saw the lie and never the correction. Drive this scenario with `curl -N .../message/stream` and read the event order: the `[Unverified` chunk must appear BEFORE the last `done`. Run with --tools file_write,create_directory,memory_store — the same probe as the other FANG-9 scenarios, so 'no tool ran' is the model's choice and not the harness's.
